title: Given 3 numbers A, B, and C representing lengths of three lines, draw a flowchart to print Yes if they can form a valid triangle and No otherwise. A triangle is valid if and only if the sum of any two sides is greater than the third (A + B > C and B + C > A and C + A > B). Start, read A, B, C, decision A + B > C AND B + C > A AND C + A > B, Yes print Yes, No print No, End. Input: 3 4 5, Expected Output: Yes (e.g. 1 2 10 -> No).
shortTitle: Form Triangle: print Yes if three lengths can form a valid triangle
keyPoints: Three lengths form a triangle if and only if the sum of every pair is strictly greater than the third side.
Three conditions joined by AND: A+B > C, B+C > A, C+A > B; if any fails the triangle is invalid.
Strict greater-than is required because equality produces a degenerate (zero-area) triangle.
For money-like BigDecimal values, use add and compareTo for exact comparison at the boundary.
Optimization: if sorted so C is the largest, only A+B > C needs to be checked, since the other two are automatic.
Validate all three lengths are positive before checking the inequality.

s1_definition.oneliner: Three lengths form a triangle only when every pair sums to strictly more than the third, checked as three AND-joined inequalities.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Triangle inequality** – A+B > C, B+C > A, C+A > B; all three must hold.
- **Strict greater-than** – equality (A+B == C) gives a degenerate triangle with zero area.
- **Single check if sorted** – if C is the max, only A+B > C is needed; the other two are automatic.
- **BigDecimal** – use `a.add(b).compareTo(c) > 0` for exact boundary comparison.
- **Positive validation** – zero or negative lengths are not valid sides.
s1_definition.analogy: National Bank of India validates that three separate limits are mutually consistent: no single limit can exceed the other two combined, mirroring the triangle inequality. For 3, 4, 5 the limits are balanced and pass. For 1, 2, 10 they are lopsided and fail.

sections.s6_takeaway:
Three lengths form a triangle if and only if the sum of every pair of sides is strictly greater than the remaining side. The condition is A+B > C, B+C > A, and C+A > B, all three joined by AND. If any single inequality fails, the three lengths cannot close into a triangle.

The comparisons must be strictly greater-than. If a pair sums to exactly the third side, the three points are collinear and the triangle is degenerate with zero area. All three sides must also be positive; a zero or negative side is meaningless.

For decimal values, use BigDecimal with add and compareTo so the comparison is exact right at the boundary, where floating-point would be risky. If sorted so the largest is last, only one inequality needs checking, but for three values all three checks are clear and cheap.

In a banking project at National Bank of India, this exact logic validated that three configuration limits were mutually balanced. A set like 3, 4, 5 passed, while 1, 2, 10 failed.

Remember one sentence: all three pair-sums must strictly exceed the third side, and equality makes it degenerate.
